question: What will Brazil's IPCA-15 monthly inflation rate be for November 2026?

calls.reasoning: November IPCA-15 (16 Oct-15 Nov collection) roughly spans late October (full Oct IPCA only +0.14%, electricity -1.92%, airfares -9.2%) and early November. Year-end IPCA consensus 5.1-5.3% vs YTD 4.10% implies Nov+Dec ~0.95-1.15pp, i.e. Nov IPCA around 0.4. Food still hot (IPC-S 1st quad Nov 0.38% with food 1.07%; analysts flag meats and El Nino), but residual electricity decline from the green flag and possibly soft fuel/airfares hold the mid-month print down. 4intelligence ~0.3%. No human market prices this monthly print; Polymarket only has annual-2026 range buckets (5.00-5.49% at 0.52), which are a mismatched contract and serve only as context. Median ~0.33.
calls.dossier:
- Resolves off IBGE IPCA-15 Nov 2026 monthly % (release 26 Nov 2026, 09:00 BRT), collection 16 Oct-15 Nov 2026; not full IPCA, not 12m. Event window: collection 16 Oct -> 15 Nov 2026; as of 16 Nov 2026 100% of collection elapsed, only publication pending.
- IPCA-15 2026: Apr 0.89, May 0.62, Jun 0.41, Jul 0.06, Aug -0.40, Sep 0.70 (consensus ~0.66 per MoneyTimes 25 Sep), Oct 0.32 (consensus ~0.44). Nov 2025 IPCA-15 was +0.20 (Oct 2025 0.18).
- Full Oct 2026 IPCA (IBGE, 12 Nov): +0.14% vs median ~0.25; electricity -1.92%, airfares -9.21%, gasoline -0.56%, food & bev +1.04%, food in natura +2.84%, tomatoes +19.57%; services 12m 5.24% (BPMoney/O Capixaba, Nov 2026).
- Aneel green tariff flag in Oct and Nov 2026 (no surcharge); analysts: electricity at tariff floor, no room for further declines (O Capixaba, Nov 2026). Part of Oct electricity decline may fall into Nov IPCA-15 window.
- FGV IPC-S 1st quadrissemana Nov 2026: +0.38% (from 0.32% end-Oct); food 0.85->1.07%, transport 0.19->0.08%, housing -0.16->-0.05% (O Povo, 9 Nov 2026).
- IPC-Fipe early Nov reportedly +0.48% with food +1.36% (CompreRural headline; year not verified).
- Mirae (Nov 2026): meats may pressure Nov/Dec; Oct relief from volatile items unlikely to repeat. Other analyst: real depreciation, negative meat seasonality, El Nino on fresh foods.
- Year-end 2026 IPCA projections 5.1-5.3% (Focus 9 Nov: 5.22%, pre-Oct-IPCA); YTD through Oct 4.10% -> implied Nov+Dec ~0.95-1.15pp. BCB raised 2026 estimate to 5.6%.
- House calls: 4intelligence ~+0.3% for Nov; Fecomercio-RS +0.38% for full Nov IPCA.
- Searched, not found: a published Broadcast/Valor consensus median for Nov 2026 IPCA-15; IPC-S 2nd quadrissemana Nov 2026; Nov IPCA-15 electricity/fuel item forecasts.
- Historical IPCA-15 consensus miss magnitude ~0.05-0.15pp (Oct 2026 -0.12, Sep 2026 +0.04).
calls.reference_class: Brazil IPCA-15 monthly prints relative to the adjacent full-IPCA months and the month's high-frequency IPC-S/IPC-Fipe readings, 2024-2026

calls.reasoning: The Nov IPCA-15 window (Oct16-Nov15) overlaps mostly with the Oct IPCA (+0.14) and early November. Downward: the rest of the green-flag electricity drop that the Oct IPCA-15 only partly caught (Oct IPCA electricity -1.92%; IPC-S electricity -1.82% in the period to ~Nov 7), plus gasoline and airfare declines. Upward: food (Oct IPCA food +1.04%, tomatoes +19.6%; IPC-S food accelerating to +1.07%). IPC-S 1st quadrissemana of Nov was +0.38%. 4intelligence ~+0.30% for the IPCA-15; Focus Nov IPCA median 0.34%. Market check: no market prices this monthly release (Polymarket lists only annual-2026 bands; 5.00-5.49% at ~0.52 implies Nov+Dec ~1.1%, a loose cross-check). Median 0.28.
calls.dossier:
- Resolves off IBGE's monthly % change in the IPCA-15 for Nov 2026 (release 26 Nov 2026, 09:00 BRT), two decimals; not the 12-month or year-to-date figures.
- Event window: price collection 16 Oct 2026 -> 15 Nov 2026 per the criteria; as of 16 Nov 2026 the collection is 100% complete and only publication is pending.
- Recent IPCA-15 prints (question background): Apr +0.89, May +0.62, Jun +0.41, Jul +0.06, Aug -0.40, Sep +0.70, Oct +0.32. Nov 2025 IPCA-15 was +0.20 (consensus 0.18; electricity -1.92% under green flag that month; food at home -0.15) [tribunadosertao, 26 Nov 2025].
- Oct 2026 IPCA (released 12 Nov): +0.14% vs median 0.25; electricity -1.92% (green flag, -0.08pp impact); gasoline -0.56% (vs expected +0.17, fuel-tax cut); airfares -9.21%; food & beverages +1.04% (tomatoes +19.57%, onions +11.29%, rice +4.81%, fresh items +2.84%); housing -0.51% [ocapixaba, Nov 2026; horadopovo, 12 Nov 2026].
- Oct 2026 IPCA-15: +0.32% vs Valor median 0.44; food +0.88%; electricity fell after the green flag began in Oct. That window started 16 Sep, so it caught only part of the flag effect [question background; spacemoney].
- Aneel kept the green flag for November (no surcharge).
- FGV IPC-S, 1st quadrissemana of Nov 2026 (period to ~7 Nov, published 9 Nov): +0.38% after +0.32% for October; food 0.85 -> 1.07%; residential electricity -2.41 -> -1.82%; tomatoes +19.75%, onions +11.44%; long-life milk -1.40%, bananas -3.22% [jornaldocomercio, 9 Nov 2026]. In October the IPC-S (+0.32) ran above the IPCA (+0.14).
- Forecasts: 4intelligence ~+0.30% for the Nov IPCA-15; Focus median for the full Nov IPCA rose 0.32 -> 0.34% (survey of 9 Nov, before the Oct IPCA print); Fecomércio-RS +0.38% for the full Nov IPCA; Focus 2026 year-end IPCA 5.22% (YTD through Oct 4.10%).
- Analysts expect the weather-driven food pressure to ease going forward [ocapixaba].
- Historical surprise size: Sep IPCA-15 +0.70 vs ~0.55 median; Oct +0.32 vs 0.44 median -> first-print misses of about +/-0.12-0.15pp.
- Searched but not found: a Broadcast/Valor consensus for the Nov 2026 IPCA-15, the 2nd-quadrissemana Nov 2026 IPC-S, and the Oct IPCA-15 airfare/gasoline breakdown.
calls.reference_class: Recent IPCA-15 prints vs. preceding full IPCA and the forecast median; November IPCA-15 seasonal readings

calls.reasoning: The collection window runs 16 Oct to 15 Nov. That covers the weak second half of October (the full October IPCA was +0.14%, with electricity -1.92%, airfares -9.2% and gasoline -0.56%) and the first half of November, still under the green tariff flag. October's IPCA-15 picked up only part of the flag effect (electricity -0.89%), so more of the electricity drop should land in this print. Food is the main upward force: October IPCA food was +1.04%, and the IPC-S food index for the first week of November was +1.07%. Headline IPC-S (+0.38%) and IPC-Fipe (+0.48%) ran 0.2-0.3pp above the IPCA in October, so I discount them. House calls: 4intelligence ~0.3% for this print, and a Focus median of 0.34% for the full November IPCA, which comes in later. A year-end consensus of ~5.2% implies roughly 0.95-1.1pp for November and December combined. Median 0.30. No human market prices this monthly print; Polymarket's annual-2026 bins are a different contract and serve only as context.
calls.reconciliation: The runs agree on almost every fact. I found no factual dispute that would move the median. One run conflated the Nov 2025 and Oct 2026 electricity figures (-1.92%), but that changes nothing. The Oct 2026 IPCA-15 electricity reading (-0.89%) versus the full October IPCA (-1.92%) supports the view that more electricity decline falls in this window, and all runs accept that. The remaining spread (medians 0.28-0.33) is a judgment call: how much to discount the IPC-S and Fipe food acceleration given their October overshoot, and how much of October's airfare and gasoline drops carry into this print. I built it from components: food ~+0.2pp, electricity ~-0.04pp, partial airfare/gasoline relief, and services/core ~0.3-0.4%. That lands near 0.28-0.32, in line with 4intelligence's ~0.3. I take 0.30 and keep a 10-90 width of ~0.32, which reflects the typical first-print miss size. I priced no mass outside the bounds, since a reading below -0.505 or above 0.905 would need a shock I can't identify in the collection window. I retrieved nothing new on this run; no web access was available.

disagreements.verdict: Building it from components and the house calls supports ~0.30. I take 0.30.

disagreements.claim: Whether more green-flag electricity decline falls in the Nov IPCA-15 window
disagreements.verdict: Supported. Oct IPCA-15 electricity -0.89% vs full Oct IPCA -1.92%, and the IPC-S first-week November electricity reading was -1.82%.

disagreements.claim: How far to trust IPC-S/Fipe acceleration as a signal for the IPCA-15
disagreements.verdict: Discounted. Both ran 0.2-0.3pp above the IPCA in October because of methodology differences on electricity and airfares.

disagreements.claim: IPC-Fipe early-November +0.48% (Run 1 had not verified the year)
disagreements.verdict: Run 3 dates it to 11 Nov 2026. Accepted, though it carries little weight.
